steps.content: War is often waged in the name of survival, but its spoils are counted in profit.

November, N.F. 114: At Fraser's instigation, numerous extremists from the farlands infiltrated DisCity to surveil its leadership movements and sow chaos.


June, N.F. 115: During the Great Expo held in DisCity, Fraser dispatched a delegation in an attempt to join the joint mining operations in the West District. At the closing ceremony, extremist Adelaide Campbell tried to capture the MBCC Chief but failed and was subsequently detained by DisCity authorities. Simultaneously, BR-005 was successfully detonated within Fraser's jurisdiction, making the shadow of war inevitable.


July, N.F. 115: Euphoria, a facility established by Fraser to infiltrate DisCity's upper echelons, was destroyed. Intelligence reports indicated that the Farland Alliance's war plans had already taken shape.

July 10, N.F. 115: The Tide of Ashes exhibited unusual activity as the "mobile" BR-005, accompanied by numerous Apostles and Aurum Secretum Warriors, swept into WhiteSands and breached multiple Ash defense lines.

August 11: Paradeisos activated BR-003 in an attempt to halt the war's escalation through the use of this catastrophe weapon.

August 21: After several days of ceasefire, the Farland Alliance forces made a desperate final push under Fraser commanders' orders, ignoring the deterrent of BR-003 and once again driving Apostle hordes into DisCity.

August 23: Through the joint efforts of the DisCorps, the FAC, and the MBCC Chief, BR-005 was shattered by the reorganized DisCity army.

In the aftermath, Fraser's military advantage collapsed instantly. The Senate abandoned their frontline commanders and Farland Alliance forces, bringing the Ash Campaign to an abrupt halt.

After the war, the Hypercube mine that should have remained on the battlefield was nowhere to be found, making its whereabouts the primary focus for all factions. However, after each side dispatched search parties for days without success, they grew increasingly pessimistic about the possibility of locating it.

September 15, N.F. 115
10:30 AM
Council Chamber, Fraser Senate

The opulent council chamber is silent but for the relentless tick of the clock counting down to the hour.
As it chimes, an electronic hum fills the air, and one by one, the spectral forms of the attendees shimmer into existence upon the encircling seats.

Their postures are a study in contrast—some ramrod straight, others draped in casual indifference—yet all are united by the golden masks of the Fraser Senate, the ultimate symbol of authority and anonymity.
The moment the last hologram solidifies, the figure at position II raises a hand, breaking the silence.

steps.speaker: II·Elliot Baker
steps.content: Everyone is present except for Adelaide Campbell. Let us begin.

steps.speaker: II·Elliot Baker
steps.content: As you are all aware, Fraser invested immense resources and took extraordinary risks in the Ash Campaign, also known as the Apostle Black Ring plan. Yet the outcome fell short of expectations. We failed to secure DisCity, lost our advantage at the critical moment, and are now compelled to sign a peace treaty... one that will undoubtedly come at significant cost to our interests. Moreover...

steps.speaker: II·Elliot Baker
steps.content: The repercussions of our defeat are already spreading to the Farland Alliance. Catastrophe intensity triggered by BR-005 continues to escalate, and more members are faltering under the strain. They are filing frequent petitions, claiming that Aurum Secretum, Hypercubes, and labor were diverted to Fraser during the war, that the Hypercubes originally slated for acquisition from DisCity are now unavailable, that... they can no longer sustain themselves and require Fraser's assistance.

steps.speaker: II·Elliot Baker
steps.content: Naturally, our propaganda efforts have never wavered. Refugees from the lesser city-states have harbored deep-seated hatred toward DisCity and placed their unconditional trust in us. They could never learn the truth about Furor. But with the collapse of our blitzkrieg strategy, compounded by DisCity's public exposure of its Black Ring weapon... fear has now begun to overshadow the hatred we so carefully cultivated. War fatigue spreads like a plague, and the hawks in every state are losing ground.

steps.speaker: II·Elliot Baker
steps.content: DisCity has also made its move. They've dispatched their new diplomat—yes, that <color=#fb9259>Margaret</color>. Her "smile diplomacy" may be ineffective in itself, but her proposals to assist in clearing Black Ring contamination and support mine construction have genuinely swayed several of the weaker states... and we cannot yet move openly against her.

steps.speaker: X·Raphael Herbert
steps.content: Useless. Every last one of them. After all the support we provided, they still managed to fail so spectacularly. Forget the sunk costs; we should freeze all further aid and investment immediately. There's no sense in pouring resources into a bottomless pit.

steps.speaker: II·Elliot Baker
steps.content: The issue is not sunk costs. If we abandon the Farland Alliance now, they won't pose any real threat; they'll simply perish in the spreading catastrophes. But without them to keep DisCity distracted, Fraser would face its full, undivided retaliation.

steps.speaker: II·Elliot Baker
steps.content: Do any of you truly believe those wartime records could absolve us completely? That warmonger Augustus has already returned. Her Rancor unit alone could carve through half of WhiteSands. When DisCity comes seeking retribution, I urge you to ask yourselves, honestly: what fate awaits us then?
Murmurs ripple through the chamber.

steps.speaker: X·Raphael Herbert
steps.content: So what you're saying is, we have no choice but to keep propping up those beggars from the Alliance?

steps.speaker: III·Valorian
steps.content: To maintain Fraser's political dominance in the farlands, this is a necessary expense. Of course... if we could immediately locate the BR-005 mineral deposits, all our current troubles would be solved, and the Farland Alliance would obediently fall in line.

steps.speaker: III·Valorian
steps.content: Until then... we should maintain minimal investment, just enough to keep them from rebelling, yet not letting them crumble completely.
[Scene Change: WhiteSands]
Deep Within WhiteSands
Relentless storms scour the desert expanse. Below, a violent Mania field churns, whipping up clouds of dust that cloak the path ahead.

Perched atop a massive boulder, a squad of Aurum Secretum Warriors keeps watch over one such disturbance. Ever since the Black Ring event, the calamities plaguing WhiteSands have only grown in ferocity. Their mission is to patrol these blighted borders, serving as sentinels against the encroaching contamination.
Suddenly, one warrior goes still. Setting aside the weapon he has been meticulously cleaning, he leans forward, his gaze piercing the dusty veil in the distance.

steps.speaker: A.S. Warrior
steps.content: Rats coming.

His teammates track his line of sight. A band of farland refugees is trekking purposefully toward the Mania field's epicenter, armed and ready—though their primitive weaponry seems almost laughable against the advanced Aurum Secretum arsenal.

steps.speaker: A.S. Warrior
steps.content: They're trying to rush a Mania field with that scrap? That's a suicide run.

steps.speaker: A.S. Warrior
steps.content: We found this place first. What's the plan, Saina? Do we move in?

steps.speaker: Saina
steps.content: Quiet. Wait a little longer.
The female warrior throws out an arm, blocking her eager companion from advancing. Her gaze remains locked on the farlanders, analytical and unmoving.

steps.speaker: Farlander A
steps.content: You really think the elders were right? That we might find Hypercubes here, where the Black Ring passed through?

steps.speaker: Farlander B
steps.content: It's a chance, not a promise. Now focus. The things in there are vicious. Is your suit sealed? The second something feels wrong, you run. Understood?

steps.speaker: Farlander A
steps.content: ...And go where?

steps.speaker: Farlander A
steps.content: Our strongholds are bled dry. All the Aurum Secretum and Hypercubes went to the war effort; all our strong backs were sent to the city. Fraser promised beating DisCity would fix everything, but we lost... And since Furor was blasted, the Tide of Ashes just keeps getting worse...

steps.speaker: Farlander A
steps.content: Heh, doesn't matter where we go, we're dead anyway. Might as well roll the dice. Maybe we get lucky and bring something home...

steps.speaker: Farlander B
steps.content: Stop with the doom and gloom! If you're done feeling sorry for yourself, let's move!
Saina watches the last farlander disappear into the swirling chaos. Silently, she begins to count.
Nothing. No one emerges.

steps.speaker: Saina
steps.content: Tch, those idiots! Move out!
On her command, the Aurum Secretum Warriors launch themselves from the boulder, diving headlong into the depths of the Mania field.
[Scene Change]
Inside the Mania field, the farlanders' gear shatters like paper against the monsters' claws.
And their lives are equally fragile.
(Red flash + blade flash, character portraits fall)

steps.speaker: Farlander A
steps.content: Why... Why... WHY WON'T THEY JUST DIE?!
(Red flash + blade flash)

steps.speaker: Farlander A
steps.content: Sob... damn it, DAMN IT!! AAAAAHHH!!!
Arcs of golden light sever the air, and the monsters fall. The farlanders can only stare, stunned, at the Aurum Secretum Warriors who now stand where the monsters had been.

steps.speaker: Saina
steps.content: Three on the left, two on the right, a big one behind. They're mine. The rest of you, stay back!

These Aurum Secretum Warriors are all marked by mutative defects, rejects from the main theater of war. Their exile is the patrol of the WhiteSands Mania fields, where they can manage the contamination but never eliminate it. Their only purpose is to occasionally rescue the foolhardy prospectors who venture in like moths to a flame.
What if I were on that front line, Saina thinks, a familiar bitterness rising, could the tide be turned? Could the farlands actually win?
But history scorns "what ifs." There is only the broken body she must carry forward, transmuting her fury into the slaughter of lesser monsters.
